title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Tests on the Transfer That Dates a Reactivation
content:
A dormant Savings & Money Market Accounts product brought back through the customer's transfer out takes its reactivation date from the latest transfer out made by telephone banking, online banking or the mobile app. This page states the two tests that transfer has to pass for its posting date to serve.

## Rule

**Alone on its date.** Looking at the latest posting date among those three channels, exactly one withdrawal through them may carry that date. If two or more withdrawals through the three channels posted on it, the ledger gives no way of telling which one came from the contact, and no reactivation date is established.

**Paid into the customer's checking.** That single withdrawal must have gone to a Personal Checking account belonging to the same customer, as the checking records confirm. Where the money went to any other account, whether another person's account or some other kind of account, no reactivation date is established.

## Input, judgement, outcome

| Withdrawals through the three channels on the latest date | Receiving account | Reactivation date |
|---|---|---|
| exactly one | a checking account of the same customer | that posting date |
| exactly one | an account of somebody else | none |
| two, one by mobile app and one by telephone banking | both to the customer's checking | none, the two cannot be told apart |

## Points of judgement

**On a shared date, does the larger transfer, or the one entered earlier in the day, win?** No. The ledger keeps no order within a day, which is exactly why a shared date establishes nothing.

**The single transfer went to the customer's savings account at another tier. Does it pass?** No. The test asks for a checking account of the same customer.
